learningObjective: Distinguish dead code elimination from unreachable code elimination and identify soundness conditions.
stem: Which statements about Dead Code Elimination (DCE) and its relationship to unreachable code elimination are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: DCE can safely remove any pure computation whose result is unused, even if the computation may throw a floating-point exception, because unused values are always safe to elide.
DCE requires SSA to be applicable; non-SSA IRs cannot support DCE because reaching definitions are ambiguous.

DCE removes instructions whose results are not used and that have no observable side effects (no memory writes, no I/O, no exceptions). An instruction that writes to memory or calls a function that may have side effects cannot be removed by DCE, even if its return value is unused.
Unreachable code elimination removes basic blocks that no execution path can reach from the entry; this is distinct from DCE, which operates on live/dead value analysis within reachable code.

explanation: A: DCE requires (unused value) AND (no observable side effects). Stores, I/O, and possibly-throwing calls remain. B: Unreachable-code elimination is control-flow based; DCE is data-flow based. They can be composed. C is wrong: FP exceptions are observable side effects (if the target environment traps or the language enforces exception semantics); removing a computation that may trap can change observable behavior. D is wrong: DCE works on non-SSA IRs with reaching-definition analysis; SSA simplifies it.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: FP exceptions can be observable; naive removal can change semantics under strict FP.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: DCE is applicable in non-SSA IRs, though SSA simplifies the analysis.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: dead value + side-effect-free are the twin conditions.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: DCE and unreachable code elimination are distinct passes.

assumptions: Program semantics may include observable side effects such as FP exceptions and I/O.
Standard IR with distinguishable pure vs side-effecting operations.
nonImplications: Does not imply that all unused loads can be removed; volatile loads are side-effecting.
Does not imply DCE eliminates all dead code in one pass; iterating with other optimizations often reveals more dead code.
